title: Define canonical Audit Log Event Schema v1 + JSON Schema artifact (required fields, taxonomy hooks, examples)
creator: Marcus Lin
description: Define the canonical, versioned audit event schema (v1) for Redwood Inference across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Deliver a JSON Schema artifact + field dictionary guidance + example events that will be used by all producers and validated by the audit-log-exporter and CI linting. This ticket is the source-of-truth for required fields, actor/target semantics, correlation IDs, and extension rules.
content:
## Background / why
Enterprise customers (especially Private deployments) are blocking on consistent audit logs that (a) cover sensitive actions end-to-end, (b) have stable semantics across services and deployment modes, and (c) are SIEM-friendly without high-cardinality surprises or PII leaks.

This ticket defines the *canonical* schema v1 that all producers MUST emit (or be normalized into), and that exporters MUST validate.

## Scope
- Canonical audit event schema v1 (field names + required/optional, semantics, constraints).
- JSON Schema artifact usable by:
  - shared producer library validation
  - audit-log-exporter validation/normalization
  - CI lints (required fields; event_type registry alignment)
- Examples for key sensitive actions (RBAC, credentials, policy/routing, retention/residency, Private install/upgrade)
- Review checklist (security/PII, SIEM compatibility, parity Hosted/Dedicated/Private)

Out of scope:
- UI work in Console (basic viewing/export config covered by other tickets)
- Full control mapping writeups (tracked separately in GRC mapping doc)

## Proposed schema structure (v1)
**Design principle:** stable top-level fields for SIEM ingestion; allow namespaced extensions for service-specific details; never log secrets; keep cardinality bounded.

### Required top-level fields (v1)
- schema_version: string
  - Format: "1.0" for initial v1 GA
  - Must be present on all events emitted by v1 producers; exporter may set during normalization for legacy producers.
- event_id: string
  - ULID preferred (lexicographically sortable); UUID allowed for producers that can’t support ULID yet.
  - Used for downstream de-duplication (at-least-once delivery) and correlation.
- event_time: string (RFC3339 / ISO-8601)
- event_type: string
  - Must be from centralized registry (ENG-4822).
  - Action-oriented naming (see taxonomy), e.g. "rbac.role.updated".
- outcome: string
  - Enum: "success" | "failure" | "unknown"
  - If failure: include error_code and error_message (bounded), and still emit the event.
- deployment_mode: string
  - Enum: "hosted" | "dedicated" | "private"
- environment: string
  - Enum: "prod" | "staging" | "dev" (Private may report "prod" but include private_cluster_id).
- tenant_id: string
- project_id: string
  - Required when action is scoped to a project; may be empty/"" only when truly tenant-global.

### Actor / identity fields (required unless explicitly not available)
- actor_type: string
  - Enum: "user" | "service_account" | "api_key" | "system" | "support" | "unknown"
- actor_id: string
  - Stable internal ID (not email). For api_key actors, use key_id not key material.
- actor_display: string
  - Optional / best-effort; should avoid PII (no raw emails). Examples: "user:1234" or "svcacct:billing-bot".
- actor_org_id: string
  - When actor is from a different org/tenant context (support access) or cross-tenant automation.
- impersonated_by: string
  - Optional. If present, include both impersonator actor fields and primary actor fields (see below note).

**Impersonation model (v1):**
- If a Redwood support operator acts as customer user, populate:
  - actor_* = effective actor (customer identity)
  - impersonated_by_* = true initiator (support identity)
  - support_ticket_id = e.g. "SUP-18421" (optional but recommended)

### Target/resource fields
- target_type: string
  - Enum-ish; align to catalog ("role", "api_key", "policy", "export_destination", "retention_policy", "private_cluster", etc.)
- target_id: string
  - Stable ID (not names). If no ID exists, use a deterministic synthetic ID (documented) or leave empty and include target_name.
- target_name: string
  - Optional; bounded; avoid arbitrary free-form.

### Request / network / correlation fields
- request_id: string (required for synchronous API/Console actions)
- trace_id: string (required when trace context available)
- admin_action_id: string
  - Required for multi-step Console workflows (e.g., “Save RBAC changes” triggers multiple backend calls). Used to tie events together.
- source_ip: string
  - Required when action originates from user traffic and IP is available at gateway.
  - Private deployments: best-effort (may be empty if operator runs locally without IP context).
- user_agent: string
  - Optional; truncated; allowlist parsing recommended.

### Change summary / diffs (bounded)
- change_summary: string
  - Human-readable, bounded (<= 1KB), no secrets.
- change_set: string
  - JSON-encoded string (not nested object in v1 doc storage); must follow a constrained mini-schema described in field dictionary.
  - Contains before/after for allowlisted fields only.

### Error fields
- error_code: string (optional)
- error_message: string (optional; truncated; avoid sensitive details)

### Extension fields
- ext_service: string
  - Producer service name (e.g., "control-plane", "console-backend", "private-installer", "policy-engine").
- ext: string
  - JSON-encoded string, namespaced keys required (e.g., "policy_engine.diff_hash").
  - Must follow cardinality rules; no raw payloads.

## JSON Schema artifact requirements
Deliver: a JSON Schema (draft 2020-12 preferred) suitable for validation in:
- Go services (control plane, gateway)
- Node/TS (console backend)
- private-installer tooling
- audit-log-exporter

Implementation constraints:
- Keep schema simple enough to avoid cross-language incompatibilities.
- Enforce enums where we can (deployment_mode, outcome, actor_type); keep event_type as string but validate via registry elsewhere.

## Example events (v1)
### 1) RBAC role updated (Console)
- event_type: "rbac.role.updated"
- actor_type: "user"
- target_type: "role"
- change_summary: "Updated role permissions"
- admin_action_id: set
- change_set: includes allowlisted fields only (e.g., permission_ids added/removed)

### 2) API key revoked (API)
- event_type: "credential.api_key.revoked"
- actor_type: "user" or "service_account" depending on initiator
- target_type: "api_key"
- target_id: key_id
- MUST NOT include key prefix/value; include only last4 or fingerprint if approved by redaction policy (ENG-4832).

### 3) Routing policy updated (Policy engine)
- event_type: "policy.routing.updated"
- target_type: "policy"
- change_summary: "Updated fallback order for model group 'general-chat'"
- change_set: bounded diff (e.g., list of model_variant_ids before/after)

### 4) Data retention setting changed
- event_type: "data.retention.updated"
- target_type: "retention_policy"
- change_set: allowlisted fields (retention_days, scope)

### 5) Private install/upgrade/rollback
- event_type: "private.cluster.upgrade.started" / ".completed" / ".failed"
- actor_type: "user" or "system" (if automated)
- target_type: "private_cluster"
- ext: includes installer_version, from_version/to_version (bounded)

## Open questions (need reviewer input before GA)
1) event_id format: ULID vs UUID — proposal: ULID recommended; schema allows both.
2) actor_display: whether to allow email — proposal: no email; keep stable IDs; email belongs in identity provider, not audit logs.
3) change_set encoding: store as JSON string vs nested object — proposal: JSON string for Linear/Confluence doc + SIEM friendliness; producers may emit nested JSON at runtime, exporter can flatten/encode depending on target.
4) source_ip availability in Private — proposal: best-effort; required for hosted/dedicated gateway-sourced actions.

## Acceptance criteria
- Confluence schema v1 document created/updated with:
  - full field dictionary (semantics + constraints)
  - explicit required vs optional
  - cardinality notes (what must be allowlisted)
  - PII/secret guidance callouts
- JSON Schema artifact published (same path) and consumable by exporter + validator library.
- At least 5 example events (above) included and validated against schema.
- Review checklist completed and signed off by Security Eng + Observability Standards + GRC.

## Review checklist
Security / privacy:
- [ ] No secrets logged (tokens, API keys, auth headers, private keys)
- [ ] PII minimized (no emails; avoid raw names; bounded user_agent)
- [ ] Redaction patterns documented for any borderline fields (ENG-4832)

SIEM compatibility:
- [ ] Stable top-level fields; avoid nested objects where common SIEMs struggle
- [ ] event_type names action-oriented and consistent
- [ ] event_id + schema_version always present

Operability / investigations:
- [ ] request_id/trace_id/admin_action_id guidance clear
- [ ] support impersonation represented (impersonated_by_*)
- [ ] outcome/error fields present even for failed attempts

Parity:
- [ ] Hosted/Dedicated/Private semantics aligned; explicitly document any gaps

## Notes
- This ticket is intentionally schema-only; producers must not invent new fields. Any service-specific details must go under ext/ext_service and must follow namespacing and cardinality rules.
- Follow-on enforcement via ENG-4822 (registry + lints) and ENG-4831 (CI gate).
